title: The Nawab seeks pardon through the Singhs

blocks.text: After failing to obtain relief from one set of holy men after another, the Nawab finally admits that ordinary remedies cannot undo what a saint has spoken. He comes to believe that Singhs alone could uplift the curse meted out by a Singh, because only the Panth can answer the wrong done to Taru Singh.
That realization drives him to summon Sikh intermediaries and plead for help. He is no longer bargaining from power, but begging for access to the mercy of the very community he persecuted.
The page marks a sharp reversal in authority. Mughal office now looks helpless, while spiritual legitimacy sits with the Khalsa and with the martyr whose curse still governs events.
